mainTopic: The death of רבי, and how long a widow has to collect her כתובה
overview: This amud finishes the story of רבי's death. The רבנן fasted and prayed for him to live. His maidservant saw how he suffered and prayed for him to rest, and she broke their prayer by throwing a jug from the roof. בר קפרא reported the death with a parable so that he would not be the one to announce it. רבי's last prayer, about toiling in Torah with all ten fingers, was answered by a בת קול, and the גמרא explains how צדיקים and angels greet a צדיק, while destroying angels meet a רשע. Then a new משנה asks how long a widow has to collect her כתובה: רבי מאיר and the חכמים give opposite 25-year rules for her father's house and her husband's house. The גמרא defends both views, with 'the load matches the camel' and the exact measure of a מקוה. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says the limit applies only without a written כתובה, while רבי אלעזר disagrees. Challenges from a lender and a divorcée are answered by saying the debtor admits the debt. A new ברייתא from the school of בר קזא begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why ציפורי was a good place for the sick רבי
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the previous sentence: ציפורי is high up and its air is pleasant.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is high up and its air is sweet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started before this section. It explains why רבי was moved to ציפורי when he became ill: the place was high and had fresh air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words are not a new teaching. They complete the earlier reason. A high place with good air was considered healthier for a sick person, which sets the scene for the story of רבי's final days.

phrases.english: which is high up, and the air is pleasant.
phrases.notes: 'Which' is ציפורי, where רבי was brought when he became ill.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמִדַּלְיָא וּבְסִים אַוֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a reason given just before this section began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציפורי was chosen for the sick רבי because it was high and had good air.

steps.title: The רבנן fast and pray on the day רבי died
steps.stepSummary: On the day רבי died, the רבנן declared a fast, prayed for mercy, and warned that anyone who announced his death would be stabbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the day that רבי died, the רבנן declared a fast and prayed for mercy. They said: Anyone who says 'רבי has died' will be stabbed with a sword.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. On the day רבי was dying, the רבנן fasted and prayed hard that he would live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their strong warning shows how badly they did not want to accept his death. They believed their prayers could hold back his death, so nobody was allowed to say that he had died.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul rested, meaning he died
They begged for mercy, they prayed
He will be stabbed with a sword

phrases.english: On that day that Rabbi died,
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name added means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: the Sages decreed a fast,
and begged for mercy, and they said:
Anyone who says "Rabbi has died"
will be stabbed with a sword.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יוֹמָא דְּנָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where רבי stayed while ill to the day he died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן fasted and prayed for רבי to live, and they forbade anyone to announce his death.

steps.title: The maidservant first prays that רבי stay alive
steps.stepSummary: רבי's maidservant went up to the roof and prayed that the people below would win out over the heavenly beings who wanted רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי's maidservant went up to the roof and said: The upper world wants רבי, and the lower world wants רבי. May it be God's will that the lower world wins over the upper world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's maidservant joins the prayers. She describes a pull between heaven and earth, and she asks that earth win, so that רבי stays alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She explains why רבי's life hangs in the balance: both heaven and earth are 'asking for' him. At this point her prayer matches the prayer of the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper ones, the heavenly beings
The lower ones, the people on earth
They will overpower or win over

phrases.english: Rabbi's maidservant went up to the roof and said:
The upper ones are asking for Rabbi,
phrases.notes: She means the heavenly beings who want רבי to join them.

phrases.english: and the lower ones are asking for Rabbi.

phrases.aramaic: יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁיָּכוֹפוּ תַּחְתּוֹנִים אֶת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים.
phrases.english: May it be God's will that the lower ones overpower the upper ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְלִיקָא אַמְּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי לְאִיגָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the maidservant's prayer next to the prayer of the רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The maidservant first prays that the people on earth win, so that רבי stays alive.

steps.title: Seeing רבי suffer, the maidservant changes her prayer
steps.stepSummary: After seeing רבי's pain each time he took off and put back on his תפילין to use the bathroom, she prayed that heaven would win.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she saw how many times he went into the bathroom, took off his תפילין, put them back on, and was in pain, she said: May it be God's will that the upper world wins over the lower world.
steps.whatsHappening: The maidservant sees how much רבי is suffering from his illness. She now prays the opposite way: that heaven wins and רבי is allowed to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His illness forced him to go to the bathroom again and again. Each time he had to take off his תפילין and then put them back on, and he was in pain. Out of compassion, she decides that letting him rest is kinder than keeping him alive in suffering.
steps.whyThisMatters: Her change of heart is the turning point of the story. It shows a prayer for a suffering person to be released, alongside the רבנן's prayer that he live.

phrases.english: Once she saw how many times
that he went into the bathroom
and took off his tefillin and put them back on,
and he was suffering,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה: יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁיָּכוֹפוּ עֶלְיוֹנִים אֶת הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
phrases.english: she said: May it be God's will that the upper ones overpower the lower ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזַאי כַּמָּה זִימְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the maidservant's earlier prayer around because of what she saw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing רבי's suffering, the maidservant prays that heaven win and that he be allowed to die.

steps.title: The jug breaks the prayers and רבי dies
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן kept praying, so the maidservant threw a jug off the roof. The noise made them stop for a moment, and רבי died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן would not stop praying for mercy. So she took a jug and threw it from the roof to the ground. They stopped praying, and רבי died.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן's prayers were still keeping רבי alive. The maidservant made a loud crash with a jug, and the prayers paused. In that moment רבי died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story assumes the רבנן's nonstop prayer was holding back רבי's death. The maidservant did not argue with them. She only interrupted their prayer for a moment, and that was enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן prayed for רבי to live. His maidservant saw his suffering and prayed for him to rest. When her jug interrupted their prayers, רבי died.
steps.confusionAlert: The jug did not hurt רבי. Its crash only made the רבנן stop praying for a moment, and that pause allowed his death.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲווֹ שָׁתְקִי רַבָּנַן מִלְּמִיבְעֵי רַחֲמֵי.
phrases.english: But the Sages would not stop begging for mercy.
She took a jug,
and threw it from the roof [to the ground].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are found in some versions but not in others.

phrases.english: They fell silent from their prayers,
and Rabbi died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הֲווֹ שָׁתְקִי רַבָּנַן מִלְּמִיבְעֵי רַחֲמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The maidservant acts on her new prayer, and the story reaches רבי's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The jug interrupted the רבנן's prayers, and in that pause רבי died.

steps.title: בר קפרא discovers that רבי has died
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן send בר קפרא to check on רבי. He finds that רבי has died, tears his garment, and turns the tear to his back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to בר קפרא: Go and check. He went and found that רבי had died. He tore his garment and turned the tear around to his back.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on right after רבי dies: בר קפרא is sent to see how רבי is doing and finds that he has passed away. He tears his clothing in mourning but hides the tear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing the garment is the usual sign of mourning for a great Torah teacher. בר קפרא hides it because of the warning in step 2 that whoever announces רבי's death would be stabbed. He keeps the custom of mourning without openly showing the news.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of רבי, known for his sharp and poetic way of speaking
He died (literally: his soul came to rest)
Tearing one's garment as a sign of mourning

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Bar Kappara:
Go and check [on Rebbi].
He went and found that he had died.
He tore his garment
and turned the tear around to his back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְבַר קַפָּרָא: זִיל עַיֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after רבי's death in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קפרא finds that רבי has died and mourns quietly by hiding his torn garment.

steps.title: בר קפרא hints at the news with a parable
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא tells the רבנן that angels and great people both held onto the holy ark, the angels won, and the ark was taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: He began and said: Angels and great people both held onto the holy ark. The angels beat the great people, and the holy ark was taken away.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא gives the news through a picture instead of saying it straight out. רבי is the holy ark, and the angels have taken him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to steps 3-5: people below and heavenly beings above were both 'pulling' on רבי. Now בר קפרא reports that the heavenly side won. Because he speaks in a parable, he never actually says 'רבי died.'

keyTerms.meaning: He began and said; the opening of a short speech
Great, righteous people on earth (literally: pillars)
The holy ark; here a picture for רבי himself

phrases.english: He began and said:
The angels and the righteous great people
held onto the holy ark.
phrases.notes: The holy ark stands for רבי, who carried the Torah.

phrases.english: The angels beat the righteous people,
and the holy ark was captured.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּתַח וַאֲמַר: אֶרְאֶלִּים וּמְצוּקִים אָחֲזוּ בַּאֲרוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding רבי dead in step 6, בר קפרא reports it to the רבנן, but only as a hint.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heavenly side won the struggle, and רבי was taken.

steps.title: The רבנן ask if רבי died, and בר קפרא lets them say it
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask, 'Did he die?' and בר קפרא answers, 'You said it, I didn't.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did he die? He said to them: You are the ones saying it, and I am not saying it.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן understand the hint and ask him plainly whether רבי died. בר קפרא makes sure that they are the ones who say the words, not him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבנן had warned that whoever announces the death would be stabbed (step 2), בר קפרא carefully avoids being 'the announcer.' The news comes out, but from the mouths of the people who made the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You are the ones saying it
And I am not saying it

phrases.english: They said to him: Did he die?
He said to them:
You are the ones saying it,
and I am not saying it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבנן respond to the parable from step 7, and בר קפרא finishes avoiding the warning from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The news of רבי's death comes out without בר קפרא being the one to announce it.

steps.title: רבי's last prayer with his ten fingers raised
steps.stepSummary: As he was dying, רבי raised his ten fingers and told ה׳ that he toiled in Torah with all ten and took no pleasure from this world even with his little finger. He asked for peace in his rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי was dying, he lifted his ten fingers toward heaven and said: Master of the world! You know that I worked hard in Torah with my ten fingers, and I did not enjoy this world even with my little finger. May it be Your will that there be peace in my rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new piece of the story: רבי's own last prayer just before he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי shows ה׳ his hands as proof: all ten fingers were used for Torah, and none were used for worldly pleasure. Even though he was very rich, he says he did not enjoy that wealth. On that basis he asks for a peaceful rest after death.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the world (a way of addressing ה׳)

phrases.english: At the time of Rebbi's passing,
he raised his ten fingers toward heaven
and said: Master of the world!
It is clear and known before You
that I toiled with my ten fingers in Torah,
and I did not enjoy [this world] even with my little finger.
May it be Your will
that there be peace in my rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי זָקַף עֶשֶׂר אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the moment of רבי's death and adds a new part of the story: his own final prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי asked for a peaceful rest because he gave all his effort to Torah and took no pleasure from this world.

steps.title: A heavenly voice answers רבי with a verse
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול answers רבי's prayer with the פסוק 'He will come in peace; they will rest on their beds.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: 'He will come in peace; they will rest on their beds.'
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers רבי's prayer from step 9 with a פסוק promising peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי asked for peace in his rest, and the answer uses those same ideas: 'peace' and 'rest.' But the פסוק switches into the plural ('they will rest'), and that is what the גמרא will ask about next.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
"He will come in peace;
they will rest on their beds."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:2

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is Heaven's answer to רבי's prayer in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven promises רבי a peaceful rest, using ישעיהו 57:2.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'their beds' instead of 'your bed'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the voice was talking about one person, רבי, so it should have said 'on your bed,' not 'on their beds.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have said 'on your bed'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the wording of the פסוק the בת קול used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer was meant for רבי alone, and the פסוק starts in the singular ('He will come'). So the switch to plural ('they will rest on their beds') looks out of place. The גמרא wants to know who 'they' are.

phrases.english: It should have said "on your bed"!
phrases.notes: Singular, since the voice was speaking about רבי alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עַל מִשְׁכָּבְךָ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plural wording of the פסוק quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plural wording 'on their beds' in the בת קול's answer to רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The message was about one person and begins in the singular, so it should stay singular: 'on your bed.'

steps.title: The צדיקים come out to greet a new צדיק, then go back to rest
steps.stepSummary: The plural fits the teaching of רבי חייא בר גמדא: when a צדיק dies, the other צדיקים go out to greet him, say 'He will come in peace,' and then they go back to rest on their beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי חייא בר גמדא, who said in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול: When a צדיק leaves the world, the angels say to ה׳: Master of the world, צדיק so-and-so is coming. ה׳ says to them: Let the צדיקים come and go out to greet him. And they say to him: 'He will come in peace,' and then they rest on their beds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11: 'they' are the צדיקים who already passed away and came out to greet רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two parts with two different subjects. 'He will come in peace' is what the צדיקים say about the new arrival. 'They will rest on their beds' is about those same צדיקים going back to their rest afterward. So the plural is not a mistake; it is about the group who welcomed רבי.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיֵּיעַ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר גַּמָּדָא.
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda.
For Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said
that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said:
When a righteous person leaves the world,
the ministering angels say
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, צַדִּיק פְּלוֹנִי בָּא.
phrases.english: Master of the world, righteous so-and-so is coming.
He says to them:
Let the righteous come and go out to greet him.
And they say to him: "He will come in peace,"
[and then] they rest on their beds.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the צדיקים who came out to greet him; after welcoming him they go back to rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיֵּיעַ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר גַּמָּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 11 by explaining who the plural 'they' refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so the plural refers to a different group of people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the whole פסוק was about רבי alone, so the plural seemed wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural refers to the צדיקים who greet the new צדיק and then go back to rest.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the בת קול's answer also told רבי he would be welcomed by the צדיקים who came before him.

steps.title: Three groups of angels greet a צדיק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that when a צדיק dies, three groups of ministering angels come out to greet him, each saying a different phrase of peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: When a צדיק leaves the world, three groups of ministering angels go out to greet him. One says to him: 'Come in peace.' One says: 'Who walks straight.' And one says to him: 'He will come in peace; they will rest on their beds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching on the same theme: how a צדיק is welcomed after he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אלעזר's picture, the first group greets him with 'Come in peace,' and the other two groups say the parts of ישעיהו 57:2. Here the greeters are angels, while in step 12 the greeters were the צדיקים themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Who walks straight, in his uprightness

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
When a righteous person leaves the world,
three groups of ministering angels
go out to greet him.
One says to him: "Come in peace."
And one says: "Who walks straight."
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the same פסוק, ישעיהו 57:2.

phrases.english: And one says to him:
"He will come in peace; they will rest on their beds."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק נִפְטָר מִן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second picture of how a צדיק is greeted, this time by three groups of angels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צדיק is welcomed by three groups of angels, each greeting him with words of peace and praise, mostly from ישעיהו 57:2.

steps.title: Three groups of destroying angels meet a wicked person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר continues: when a רשע dies, three groups of destroying angels go out to him, each saying a harsh פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a רשע is lost from the world, three groups of destroying angels go out to meet him. One says: 'There is no peace, says ה׳, for the wicked.' One says to him: 'You will lie down in pain.' And one says to him: 'Go down and lie with the uncircumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר finishes his teaching with the opposite case: what happens when a wicked person dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a mirror image of step 13. Instead of three groups offering peace and rest, three groups of destroying angels say there is no peace and that the רשע will lie down in pain and disgrace. Even the wording is different: the צדיק 'leaves' (נפטר), while the רשע 'is lost' (נאבד).
steps.whatToRemember: A צדיק is greeted with peace (by צדיקים and by three groups of ministering angels), while a רשע is met by three groups of destroying angels saying there is no peace. רבי, who gave all ten fingers to Torah, received the promise of peace.

phrases.english: When a wicked person is lost from the world,
three groups of destroying angels
go out to meet him.
One says:
"There is no peace, says ה׳, for the wicked."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:22

phrases.english: And one says to him: "In pain he will lie down."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 50:11

phrases.english: And one says to him:
"Go down and lie with the uncircumcised."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 32:19

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהָרָשָׁע נֶאֱבָד מִן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבי אלעזר's teaching; the mirror image of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רשע is met by three groups of destroying angels, each saying a פסוק of no peace and disgrace.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's view on a widow's time limit
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. According to רבי מאיר, a widow living in her father's house can collect her כתובה forever. A widow living in her husband's house can collect only for 25 years, because by then her giving from the orphans' property adds up to the value of her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: As long as she lives in her father's house, she can always collect her כתובה. As long as she lives in her husband's house, she can collect her כתובה only for twenty-five years, because in twenty-five years she has enough time to do favors worth as much as her כתובה. These are the words of רבי מאיר, who said them in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The story about רבי's passing is over, and a brand-new משנה starts. It asks how long a widow has to collect her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she lives in her husband's house, she runs things there and can give from the orphans' property to others. Over 25 years, רבי מאיר assumes, that giving adds up to the value of her כתובה, so she has nothing left to collect. In her father's house she isn't using their property, so there is no time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract. It promises the wife a payment when the marriage ends, for example when her husband dies.
A favor or kindness, here meaning giving things to others
In the name of (quoting someone else)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
As long as she is in her father's house
phrases.notes: 'She' is a widow who is being supported by her late husband's heirs.

phrases.english: she collects her כתובה forever
As long as she is in her husband's house

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ עַד עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים
phrases.english: she collects her כתובה until twenty-five years
because there is in twenty-five years
enough time for her to do favors equal to her כתובה
phrases.notes: He means she gives things away from the orphans' property, until it adds up to what she was owed.

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי מאיר

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: who said it in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהִיא בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ, גּוֹבָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic. It is not connected to the story about רבי's passing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר: in her father's house she can collect forever. In her husband's house she can collect only for 25 years, because by then her giving has used up the value of her כתובה.

steps.title: The חכמים hold the opposite view
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים flip רבי מאיר's rule. In her husband's house she can collect forever. In her father's house she can collect only for 25 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: As long as she lives in her husband's house, she can always collect her כתובה. As long as she lives in her father's house, she can collect her כתובה only for twenty-five years.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר and turn his rule exactly upside down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In her husband's house the heirs are supporting her, so she is embarrassed to take them to court. Her silence there does not show that she gave up her claim, so there is no time limit. In her father's house nothing stops her from suing, so if 25 years pass and she never sued, we assume she gave up her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis say. This introduces the majority view that disagrees with the first view.

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same two places and the same 25 years, but they swap which place gets the limit. Their reasons are also different. רבי מאיר thinks she has used up the money. The חכמים think she has given up her claim.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: father's house means forever, husband's house means 25 years. חכמים: husband's house means forever, father's house means 25 years.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say
As long as she is in her husband's house
she collects her כתובה forever
As long as she is in her father's house

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ עַד עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: she collects her כתובה until twenty-five years

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר and reverses his rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים: in her husband's house she can collect forever. In her father's house she can collect only for 25 years.

steps.title: If the widow dies, her heirs have twenty-five years
steps.stepSummary: If the widow dies, her own heirs can still claim her כתובה, but only for 25 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she died, her heirs can bring up her כתובה for twenty-five years.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with one more case: the widow died before she collected her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her right to the money passes to her heirs. They also have a 25-year window to claim it. After that, they lose the claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Heirs, the people who inherit from someone
Mention or bring up, meaning they make a claim for it

phrases.english: If she died
her heirs bring up her כתובה
until twenty-five years

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתָה — יוֹרְשֶׁיהָ מַזְכִּירִין כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final case to the משנה: the widow has died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her heirs can claim her כתובה for 25 years.

steps.title: אביי asks how one 25-year limit fits both poor and rich
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבי מאיר's reason. A poor woman has a small כתובה, and a very rich woman like מרתא בת בייתוס has a huge one. How can both take exactly 25 years to give away the value of their כתובה?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: אביי said to רב יוסף: The poorest woman in ישראל gets twenty-five years, and מרתא בת בייתוס also gets twenty-five years?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. אביי questions רבי מאיר's reason for the 25-year rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said that in 25 years a widow's giving adds up to the value of her כתובה. But the value of a כתובה is very different for different women. A poor woman's small כתובה should be used up much sooner, and a rich woman's huge one much later. So one fixed number of years seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: A famously wealthy woman, used here as the example of a very large כתובה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
אביי said to רב יוסף
The poorest woman in ישראל
gets until twenty-five years
and מרתא בת בייתוס
also gets until twenty-five years?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי מאיר gave in the משנה for the 25-year rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reason that 25 years of giving equals the value of a widow's כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The value of a כתובה depends on how wealthy the woman is. So the time it takes to use it up should also be different for each woman, not a fixed 25 years for everyone.

steps.title: The load matches the camel
steps.stepSummary: The answer to אביי: a rich woman spends more and a poor woman spends less, so both use up their כתובה in about 25 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to the camel is its load.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's question from the last step with a short saying: a bigger camel carries a bigger load.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי asked how a small כתובה and a huge כתובה could both be used up in the same 25 years. The answer is that spending grows with wealth. A rich woman like מרתא בת בייתוס gives away more each year, so her bigger כתובה also runs out in about 25 years.

keyTerms.meaning: A load or burden that is carried

phrases.english: He said to him:
According to the camel is the load.
phrases.notes: He means a rich woman spends and gives away more than a poor one, so the 25 years fits both.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְפוּם גַּמְלָא שִׁיחְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenge's assumption that every woman spends the same amount; spending is proportional to wealth.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fixed 25-year limit seems unfair, because a poor woman would use up her small כתובה faster than a rich woman would use up her big one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each woman spends according to her wealth, so 25 years is a fair limit for everyone in רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps רבי מאיר's reasoning standing: the 25 years is based on how much a woman gives away, and that amount matches her wealth.

steps.title: Does she lose part of her כתובה if only part of the time passed?
steps.stepSummary: A question: according to רבי מאיר, if only some of the 25 years have passed, does the widow lose a matching part of her כתובה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: According to רבי מאיר, what is the law about dividing her כתובה by the years that have passed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question based on רבי מאיר's reasoning about the 25 years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says that after 25 years, what she has given away equals her כתובה. If so, maybe after, say, half the time, she has used up half and loses half. The question is whether the loss works bit by bit, or only all at once at 25 years.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked (among the חכמים)
That she divides (the כתובה by the years that have passed)

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
According to Rabbi Meir, what is the law: does she divide?
phrases.notes: Divide here means she loses part of her כתובה to match the part of the 25 years that has already gone by.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מַהוּ שֶׁתְּשַׁלֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי מאיר's reasoning, which step 19 just defended, and asks a further question about it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, in רבי מאיר's view, a widow loses a proportional part of her כתובה when only part of the 25 years has passed.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question is left standing (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא could not find an answer to the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question is left without a decision. We do not know whether, in רבי מאיר's view, she loses her כתובה bit by bit.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 20 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a widow loses part of her כתובה for part of the 25 years, according to רבי מאיר, stays undecided.

steps.title: Can one moment after sunset really cost her the whole כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף about the חכמים' 25-year limit: if she comes before sunset on the last day she collects, but just after sunset she does not? Did she give up her rights in that tiny moment?
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: As long as (she is in her husband's house, she collects at any time). אביי said to רב יוסף: If she came before sunset (at the end of the 25 years), she collects her כתובה, but after sunset she does not collect? In that tiny bit of time, did she give it up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the חכמים' opinion in the משנה, and אביי challenges how strict their 25-year cutoff is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חכמים' view, a widow in her father's house loses her כתובה after 25 years, because we assume she gave up on it. אביי argues that it makes no sense to say she gave it up in the last few minutes. Someone who did not give it up a moment before sunset surely did not give it up a moment after.

keyTerms.meaning: A little bit, a tiny amount (of time)
She gave it up, gave up her rights to it

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: As long as.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the start of the חכמים' words in the משנה from step 16.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
If she came before sunset,
phrases.notes: He means sunset on the very last day of the 25 years.

phrases.english: she collects her marriage contract;
but after sunset she does not collect?
In that tiny bit of time, did she give it up?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: אֲתַאי קוֹדֶם שְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי מאיר's opinion and returns to the חכמים' opinion from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' rule that a widow in her father's house collects only within 25 years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 25-year rule is based on the idea that she gave up her rights. It seems unreasonable that this happens in the single moment between before sunset and after sunset.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not asking about רבי מאיר here. He is asking about the חכמים, who apply the 25 years to a widow in her father's house.

steps.title: Every measure of the חכמים is exact, like a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers yes: all measures of the חכמים have exact limits. A מקוה with 40 סאה works, but one missing even a tiny bit does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. All the measures of the חכמים are like this. In 40 סאה (of water) a person may immerse. In 40 סאה missing a tiny bit, he cannot immerse in them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף agrees that one moment does make the difference, and he backs it up with the example of a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any fixed limit has to end somewhere, so the last moment always decides. A מקוה needs 40 סאה of water. Even if it is missing only a tiny amount, it is not kosher for טבילה. The 25 years of the חכמים works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: The fixed measures set by the חכמים
A measure of volume; a מקוה needs 40 of them
He immerses (in a מקוה to become טהור)

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים' 25-year limit is exact: before sunset of the last day she collects, after sunset she does not. Fixed measures of the חכמים always have a sharp cutoff, like the 40 סאה of a מקוה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
All the measures of the Sages are like this.
In forty se'a, one immerses;
phrases.notes: This is talking about a מקוה, which needs 40 סאה of water.

phrases.english: in forty se'a missing a tiny drop,
he cannot immerse in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, כׇּל מִדַּת חֲכָמִים, כֵּן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the result אביי found strange and explains it as a general rule: fixed measures have exact limits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seems unreasonable that one moment after sunset could cost her the whole כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Yes, it can. All the חכמים' measures have exact cutoffs, just as a מקוה missing a drop of its 40 סאה is not kosher.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general principle across הלכה: when the חכמים set a measure, it is exact, even if the line looks tiny.

steps.title: With a כתובה document in hand, she collects forever
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, in his father's name, limits the 25-year rule to a widow who has no written כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי testified before רבי in his father's name. The 25-year rule was taught only when she has no כתובה document. If she has one, she can collect her כתובה forever.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement narrows the 25-year rule we have been discussing. It applies only to a widow who does not hold a written כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a document, we assume that after many years of silence she gave up her claim. A written document in her hand shows she kept her claim alive, so time does not erase it.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught this in the case of...
is in her possession (literally: comes out from under her hand)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei testified before Rabbi,
that he said in the name of his father:
They taught this only
phrases.notes: 'This' is the 25-year limit on collecting a כתובה that we have been discussing.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדֶיהָ,
phrases.english: where she does not have a כתובה document in her possession,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדֶיהָ
phrases.english: but where she does have a כתובה document in her possession,
she collects her כתובה forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the exact edge of the 25 years to the question of which cases the limit covers at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 25-year limit applies only when there is no written כתובה. A widow who holds the document collects forever.

steps.title: Even with the document, only 25 years
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees and says the 25-year limit applies even when she holds her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: even if she has her כתובה document, she can collect only for 25 years.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion disagrees with the one just stated. For רבי אלעזר, holding the document does not help her after 25 years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that a widow's long silence shows she gave up her claim, whether or not she has the paper. So the question is whether a written document can protect her from being treated as having given up.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדֶיהָ
phrases.english: Even if she has a כתובה document in her possession,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ גּוֹבָה אֶלָּא עַד עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: she collects only up to twenty-five years.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 25-year limit applies even when she holds the כתובה document.

steps.title: A lender collects late, but a widow is assumed to give up
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת challenges רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי: a ברייתא says only a בעל חוב with a document keeps his claim, which implies a widow with a document loses hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: a lender collects even if he never mentioned the debt. What is the case? If he has no document, what is he collecting with? So he must hold the document. It is a lender who does not give up his money, but a widow does give up her claim!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks the view that a widow holding her כתובה collects forever. He uses a teaching about a lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא must be talking about a lender who holds a document. Even so, it stresses that a lender keeps his claim because a lender does not forgive debts. That suggests a widow, even with a document, is assumed to have given up her claim, which goes against רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection from a source
someone likely to forgive or give up a claim

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
A creditor collects even without having mentioned the debt.
What is the case?
If he does not hold a document,
with what is he collecting?
Rather, he holds a document:

phrases.aramaic: וּבַעַל חוֹב הוּא דְּלָאו בַּר אַחוֹלֵי הוּא,
phrases.english: and it is a creditor who is not one to forgive,
but a widow has given it up!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion stated in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's ruling that a widow with a document collects forever.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא must involve a lender with a document, yet it gives his reason as 'a lender does not forgive.' That implies a widow with a document is assumed to forgive.

steps.title: The lender's case is where the borrower admits
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers his own challenge: the ברייתא is about a lender with no document, whose borrower admits the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he answered it: really, the lender has no document. The case is where the borrower admits he owes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת removes his own challenge by reading the ברייתא as a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step-26 challenge depended on the claim that the lender must hold a document. רב ששת shows he can collect without one when the borrower admits the debt. So the ברייתא says nothing about someone who holds a document, and there is no proof that a widow with a document loses her claim.

keyTerms.meaning: raises a challenge and answers it
here, what case are we dealing with?

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
Actually, he does not hold a document,
and here, what are we dealing with?
Where the debtor admits.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case in the ברייתא (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lender must hold a document, because otherwise he would have nothing to collect with.
steps.terutzMaskana: He has no document, and he collects because the borrower admits the debt. So nothing can be learned about a widow who holds a document.

steps.title: A גרושה is like a lender, but a widow gives up
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge from רבי אלעא: a divorced woman collects like a lender, which suggests a widow holding her כתובה is assumed to give it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעא said they teach: a divorced woman is like a lender. What is the case? If she does not hold a כתובה, what is she collecting with? So she must hold a כתובה. It is a divorced woman who does not give up her claim, but a widow does give it up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source against רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. It is a teaching of רבי אלעא about a divorced woman, built the same way as רב ששת's challenge in step 26. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman collects her כתובה with her document, so the case must be one where she holds it. The teaching stresses that a divorced woman is not one to give up her claim. That implies a widow does give hers up even when she holds the document, which is the same problem as before.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say...? (opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge has the same shape as the one in step 26: 'without a document, what would she collect with?' The next step answers it the same way step 27 did, that the debtor admits the debt.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ela say: they teach:
A divorcée is like a creditor.
What is the case?
If she does not hold a כתובה,
with what is she collecting?
Rather, is it not that she holds a כתובה,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְרוּשָׁה הִיא דְּלָאו בַּת אַחוֹלֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: and it is a divorcée who is not one to give up,
but a widow has given it up!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא שׁוֹנִין גְּרוּשָׁה הֲרֵי הִיא כְּבַעַל חוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 27 removed the challenge from the lender, this brings a new source with the same problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's ruling that a widow with a document collects forever.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גרושה must hold her כתובה to collect, yet only she is described as not giving up her claim. That implies a widow holding her כתובה is assumed to give hers up.

steps.title: The husband admits the debt
steps.stepSummary: The divorced woman in the ברייתא collects only because her husband admits he owes her the כתובה, even though she has no document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where the one who owes admits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אלעא's challenge from Step 28. It uses the same answer רב ששת gave in Step 27: the case is one where the debtor admits he owes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the divorcée collects because she holds a written כתובה, which would suggest a widow holding hers is the one who loses. The גמרא says the divorcée has no document at all. She collects only because her husband admits the debt, so nothing can be learned about a widow who holds her document.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: the same answer as before applies
The one who owes; here, the husband

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the second challenge to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's view that the 25-year limit applies only to a widow without a written כתובה.

phrases.english: Here too,
it is where the one who owes admits it.
phrases.notes: The one who owes is the husband. He admits he owes his divorced wife her כתובה, even though she has no document.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי כְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of רבי אלעא in Step 28 by applying the answer from Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the source is about a debtor who admits the debt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The divorcée collects because she holds her written כתובה, so a widow holding hers must be the one who loses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The divorcée has no document and collects only because the husband admits the debt, so no inference about a widow holding a document follows.

steps.title: A teaching from the school of בר קזא begins
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts quoting a ברייתא taught by רב יהודה בר קזא about a widow who demanded her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רב יהודה בר קזא taught in the ברייתא of the school of בר קזא: If she demanded her כתובה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by bringing a new ברייתא. Only the opening words appear on this amud, and the ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new source, not a reply to the earlier challenges. It opens with a widow who demanded payment of her כתובה. It is about to explain how such a demand affects the 25-year rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה
Of the school of בר קזא
